the left prefrontals are important for self-prioritizing attentional control and the right inferior temporal regions are important for the representation of self in the brain.
the right temporal lobe, in particular the hippocampus, is critical for the self-prioritizing effect, whereas the left prefrontality is critical for the modulation of self-prioritized responses.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the self-bias is not a single phenomenon but rather it is composed of two different components, a right hemisphere component that is associated with face recognition, and a left hemisphere component that is linked with executive processes.
self-prioritisation is a complex process that involves multiple brain regions, and that lesions can lead to hypo- as well as hyper-self-biased responses.
